findings.symptom: The displayed lower-bound expression uses raw ASCII `sqrt(n/(60 ln 2))/t` in the statement; the corresponding rearranged inequality in proof line 50 is typeset. The notation is legible but inconsistent with the proof and the mathematical title.

diagram_candidates.verdict: potentially warranted; optional and not required for proof validity
diagram_candidates.source_claim: A closed convex body contains B(0,r) and lies in B(0,R); its lower height h(y) is convex and Lipschitz on B(0,r/2), weak-membership IN/OUT answers bracket h(y), and binary search returns an approximation.
diagram_candidates.why: The statement combines geometric containment, a lower boundary graph, vertical membership queries, and a one-dimensional bracket update. A cross-section makes the roles of the radii and the IN/OUT inequalities easier to follow.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: Draw a labeled planar cross-section of K between the inner and outer balls, the projected domain C, lower boundary t=h(y), a query point (y,t) on the vertical line, and an interval [ell,u] for the binary search. Mark the two weak-membership implications as bounds on t relative to h(y), with the signs IN: t≥h(y)−3Rε/r and OUT: t≤h(y)+2Rε/r. Label it schematic and do not use the picture as proof.
diagram_candidates.certainty: pedagogical candidate, not a defect; no current diagram to validate

diagram_candidates.kind: TikZ quantum circuit with address and target registers
diagram_candidates.source_claim: The one-query procedure applies H^{⊗n} to the address, X then H to target, one standard XOR oracle on (A,T), H^{⊗n} to A, then measures A and outputs a.
diagram_candidates.why: This is a compact canonical circuit with two distinct registers and a single oracle call; the prose specifies a complete gate order suitable for a legible circuit schematic.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: Draw n address wires A_1,…,A_n and one target wire T; initialize |0^n⟩|0⟩; show H on every address wire, X then H on T, the single U_{f_a} box spanning A and T, H on every address wire, and measurement only on A with classical output a. Keep the target unmeasured and identify its |−⟩ phase-kickback state after X then H.
diagram_candidates.certainty: pedagogical candidate, not a defect; no current diagram to validate
